props.text:
## Compound interest

A principal $P$ invested at annual rate $r$ grows to

$$A(t) = P\left(1 + \tfrac{r}{100}\right)^{t}$$

after $t$ years. The growth itself earns interest, which is why the curve below bends upward. Drag the sliders on the next card and watch it react.
At **{{r}}%**, an initial **{{P}}** roughly doubles every **{{doubling}}** years. Same card, same variables: the sliders above write $P$ and $r$, everything below reads them.

props.q: You invest at **6%** compounded annually. About how long until your money doubles?
props.explanation: Rule of 72: 72 / 6 = 12 years. The exact answer, ln 2 / ln 1.06, is 11.9 years.
